title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Dispersion — 2022
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What is meant by dispersion of light? Why does white light disperse into seven colours when passed through a glass prism?
questions.solution:
**Dispersion:** The splitting of a beam of white light into its constituent seven colours (VIBGYOR) when it passes through a dispersive medium is called dispersion.

**Reason:** The refractive index $\mu$ of the glass is **different for different colours**, and since $\mu$ depends on the wavelength (or frequency) of light, violet light (shortest wavelength) is deviated most and red light (longest wavelength) is deviated least.
$$\mu_v > \mu_r$$
Therefore the band of colours fans out and they appear separately on the screen.
questions.knowledgeNote: Dispersion happens because refractive index of the medium varies with the wavelength of light.
questions.answer: **Dispersion of light:** the splitting of white (composite) light into its constituent colours when it passes through a refracting medium — red bends least, violet most, giving the spectrum. **Why it happens:** the **refractive index of a material depends on the wavelength (colour) of light** (normal dispersion: n decreases as λ increases, because higher frequencies interact more strongly with the medium's electrons). White light contains all wavelengths; in the prism each colour obeys Snell's law sin i/sin r = n_λ with its own n: violet (largest n ≈ 1.53) refracts most, red (smallest n ≈ 1.51) least. Since the prism's faces are not parallel, the tiny per-refraction differences are **not cancelled on exit** — the colours emerge at different angles and spread into the spectrum (seven colours: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red). **Deep point:** dispersion needs two ingredients — wavelength-dependent n *and* non-parallel surfaces; a glass slab refracts all colours by different amounts too, but its parallel faces recombine them, so no spectrum appears.
